title: Doctor runtime inventory
description: Objective: give Linux/macOS packaging conformance a real production doctor surface for exact engine and tool observations. Deliverable: a focused daemon recovery runtime-inventory module, composition into doctor.report_recovery_state, public daemon export, and tests. NOT in scope: changing recovery authority, running platform conformance, adding test:fault, editing package-manager pins, or inferring unavailable versions. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-runtime-inventory.* plus the minimal doctor-commands/index/test wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: doctor.report_recovery_state returns a deeply frozen runtime inventory containing the declared Node engine range, observed Node runtime, declared pnpm version, observed platform/architecture, and any explicitly supplied build-tool versions, each with PROVEN or UNKNOWN truth.

Missing, malformed, contradictory, or stale version observations fail closed with a stable DOCTOR_RUNTIME_* reason code and the DOCTOR_RUNTIME layer; tests assert both code and layer rather than only refusal.
The inventory composes into the existing report-only doctor path without changing proposal commands, confirmation requirements, recovery authority, or existing DOCTOR_REQUEST_* refusal ordering.
@moe/daemon publicly exposes the runtime inventory/report types and production constructor, and its raw Node runtime-entrypoint test proves the export is defined.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0; package.json remains the single source for the already-declared Node/pnpm pins and no host fact is guessed.
taskRails: Read versions from explicit immutable observations and declared package metadata; never turn an absent executable/tool into a guessed version.
Keep doctor-commands.ts below the production-file line cap by placing runtime inventory validation/composition in its own focused module.
This task creates the production reporting capability only; Linux/macOS conformance remains a separate real-host proof.
